chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al-Fadl ibn Yunus, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about lifting the coffin by its four corners. He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are in a place of dissimulation (taqiyyah), begin with the right hand, then the right leg, then return from your place to the right side of the deceased, not passing behind his leg at all until you face the coffin. So take his left hand, then his left leg, then return from your place and do not pass behind the coffin at all until you face it, doing as you did first.'

So if you are not practicing dissimulation in it, then the lifting of the coffin according to the Sunnah is to begin with the right hand, then the right leg, then the left leg, then the left hand, until you circle around it.

key_terms.تَرْبِيعِ الْجَنَازَةِ: Lifting the coffin by its four corners
key_terms.مَيَامِنِ الْمَيِّتِ: The right side of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method for carrying a coffin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific mechanics of 'tarbi' (carrying the coffin by its four corners), distinguishing between a method of dissimulation (taqiyyah) and the standard Sunnah. In the standard practice, the carriers move in a continuous circular motion around the deceased, a ritual act that reflects the reverence due to the body and aligns with the Prophetic tradition of honoring the dead. The distinction highlights how Shia jurisprudence adapts ritual precision to contexts of religious caution or normative practice.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al Fazl Bin Yunus who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about (lifting of the) four corners of the coffin. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you were in a place of dissimulation, so begin with the right hand, then with the right leg, then return from your place to the right hand side of the deceased, not passing behind his leg at all until you face the coffin. So take to his left hand, then his left hand, then return from your place and do not pass behind the coffin at all until you face it, doing just as you did firstly.

So if there does not happen to be dissimulation, then the (procedure) of lifting up all four corners of the coffin, which is of the Sunnah, is to life-up the corner where the right hand (of the dead person) is.  Thereafter, one should lift-up the corner where the right leg is, then the left leg and finally lift-up the corner where the left hand is until the circle is complete. (Anticlockwise movement starting from front end giving right shoulder)
